answer: The nectar cap is applied at intake and horizon exposes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a fleet in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a ember tag. That is 27 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
